Each card carries the action the review policy would take if these 10 rings were tonight's queue and an analyst had 120 minutes, with a wrongly held customer assumed to lose 10% of their value. The two figures behind it are shown so a reviewer can see which one the recommendation turned on.
These are leads for a human to review, not verdicts. Rupee figures are counts multiplied by an assumed value — this dataset ships no monetary amounts — so they rank rings against each other and mean nothing in absolute terms.

The clusters it left alone, and why

2,444 of 2,446 co-located groups whose labelled members are overwhelmingly normal — hostels, shared offices, joint families — have no member in any ring (99.92% of them)
the groups it left alonethe ones it touched
mean account score0.150.29
kinds of shared entity1.761.50
edges inside the group147.65112.50
The separation is the account score, not the structure. Groups that were left alone are actually more densely connected and share more kinds of entity — which is exactly what a hostel looks like. What keeps them out of a ring is that their members do not behave like fraudsters, and that is the whole argument for scoring accounts before looking for dense structure rather than after.
Toucheda group of 23 sharing one entity, 93% of its labelled members good9 of them ended up in a ring (39%), mean score 0.318
Toucheda group of 19 sharing one entity, 92% of its labelled members good1 of them ended up in a ring (5%), mean score 0.258
These two are the failures, shown because a page that only listed the successes would be worth less. Both are groups where the members really did score high, so the score cut-off let them through — the cost of the ordering that makes everything else work.
